main_issue: Zero representative cases and zero evidence refs. The mechanism description (cyclic links, null entries, unbounded extraction loops causing DoS) is conceptually coherent, but without a single source-to-sink trace showing a concrete vulnerable extraction loop, null-sensitive parser, or unbounded recursion, the boundary is purely theoretical. The ledger row itself confirms this in all four guard fields — source_shape, sink_or_sensitive_effect, exploit_precondition, and safe_fix_semantics all explicitly state evidence is absent.

The three representative cases share a clean mechanism: archive entry name → path resolution beneath an extraction root → filesystem write/create before a same-path containment guard. The source shape (iterate archive entries, combine entry name with temp/extraction dir), sink shape (FileOutputStream, Files.copyFile, directory/symlink creation on the resolved path), missing guard (no normalized/canonical containment check applied to the exact destination used by the write), and exploit precondition (attacker-supplied archive with malicious entry names) are all coherent. The boundary text is well-scoped — it explicitly covers traversal components, absolute paths, separator variants, and prefix-confusion, which distinguishes it from a generic path-traversal guideline. The DSpace SAF import case uses string concatenation rather than File API, but the mechanism pattern is the same. The boundary is actionable with concrete safe-fix semantics.
